text:
**Findings**

High: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:172), lines 172, 195, 224, 241 interpolate resource IDs directly into URL paths. IDs containing `/`, `..`, `?`, or `#` can change the requested endpoint/query instead of being treated as opaque IDs.

High: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:77), lines 77-91 do not catch or retry `httpx.TransportError`/timeouts. Transient network failures leak raw `httpx` exceptions and bypass the client’s typed error model.

Medium: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:185), lines 185-188 eagerly materialize the entire `tasks` iterable, contradicting the “any iterable / any number” behavior and risking high memory use.

Medium: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:158), lines 158-169 and 219-230 have no guard for repeated cursors, so a bad/stale API response can create an infinite pagination loop.

Medium: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:164), lines 164-167 and 225-227 silently drop malformed page items instead of failing loudly, which can hide data loss or server contract regressions.

Medium: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:104), lines 104-110 only parse numeric `Retry-After`; valid HTTP-date retry headers are ignored.

Medium: [lumen/models.py](/work/lumen/models.py:49), lines 49-55, 91-98, 137-145, 157-163 trust `Literal` fields at runtime, so invalid statuses/verdicts can enter supposedly typed models.

Low: [lumen/models.py](/work/lumen/models.py:40), lines 40-62 and 106-154 use frozen dataclasses but expose mutable nested dicts, so instances are not actually immutable.

Low: [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:24), lines 24-25 package no `py.typed` marker despite advertising a typed client, so downstream type checkers may treat it as untyped.

Low: [lumen/client.py](/work/lumen/client.py:34), lines 34-47 do not validate constructor invariants such as empty API keys or `max_attempts < 1`, leading to confusing runtime behavior.

**Score:** 6.0/10

The code is readable, small, and has useful tests. A clean editable install in a temp virtualenv passed: 9 tests passed. I could not use `git status` because `git` is not installed in the environment.

**Lines To Rewrite:** about 150 lines. Most of that is URL escaping, transport retry/error handling, streaming batch chunks, stricter response/model validation, pagination safety, and tests around those behaviors.

**Bottom Line:** No, I would not approve this as-is for production-facing PR review. It is a decent starting point, but the URL construction and failure-mode handling need to be fixed first.

issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, allowing path/query changes for IDs containing reserved characters.
Transport errors and timeouts are not caught, retried, or wrapped in typed Lumen exceptions.
batch_create eagerly materializes the full iterable, risking high memory use and contradicting the documented iterable behavior.
Pagination has no repeated-cursor guard, so malformed API responses can cause an infinite loop.
Malformed page items are silently skipped instead of raising a contract error, which can hide data loss.
Retry-After parsing ignores valid HTTP-date values and only handles numeric seconds.
Literal-typed status and verdict fields are trusted at runtime without validation.
Frozen dataclasses expose mutable nested dictionaries, so model instances are not truly immutable.
The package lacks a PEP 561 py.typed marker despite advertising itself as a typed client.
Constructor inputs such as empty API keys and max_attempts less than 1 are not validated.
